answer: Agents servicing a beacon and lantern network along a basalt coast must lock ten tokens for each concurrent job reservation. The ledger atomically escrows separate collateral before assigning each slot and unlocks it only when that reservation ends. An operator with fifty tokens can hold at most five slots, whether it uses one account or a thousand aliases; there is no free per-account quota. This bounds concurrent reservation spam rather than proving unique identities. Wealthy attackers can still hoard slots, and honest newcomers need capital.
